jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Quality Engineer (CIQE)
jobs.description:
Primary Function of the Position
Ensure that quality systems, products, and manufacturing processes comply with quality standards by supporting and driving improvements in the organization and in accordance with international industry practices and regulations (e.g., ISO 13485, 21CFR820).  Meet objectives, provide support and expertise in NC & corrective and preventive action (CAPA) process and system and implementing actions to drive the improvement. S/he will partner with subject matter experts on various NC/CAPA activities in addition to supporting other improvement initiatives.  S/he will evolve existing processes/systems to ensure timely escalation, identification, and robust investigation of product quality and compliance issues within a closed-loop quality management system.
Essential Job Duties
- Support and comply with Company and Site’s Health, Safety, and Environmental programs and requirements, including:

- - Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as applicable.

- Use devices, accessories, tools, and equipment according to the process, verifying that they are in good condition for use and reporting those that are in poor condition for repair.

- Communicates unsafe acts or conditions to their superiors.

- Participates in the Health, Safety, and Environment courses established.

- Maintains order and cleanliness in the workstation (5S) under responsibility.

- Complies with health regulatory and International Standard (ISO13485) requirements, Company and site policies, operating procedures, processes, and task assignments.

- Participate in or lead completion of NC & CAPA projects, assuring compliance, quality, and timeliness of records.

- Communicate confidently and effectively with all levels of management, peers, and key stakeholders, including timely escalation of quality issues.

- Lead and collaborate with cross-functional teams using various methodologies (e.g., Six Sigma root cause analysis/problem-solving skills).

- Independently investigate, gather data, trends, and perform preliminary analysis.

- Process requests, ensuring subject matter experts and action item owners are assigned and provide timely responses in alignment with quality goals.

- Leads meetings and communications for NC/CAPA updates, information, and concerns.

- Responsible for assisting with metrics and reporting in accordance with established procedures.

- Support the team in delivering and overseeing the NC & CAPA training program.

- Assist in initiating, processing, and completing NC & CAPA records in the electronic system.

- Execute and provide on-time completion of Quality Engineering deliverables.

- Provide support and NC’s or CAPA’s process/system subject matter expertise during audits and inspections.

- Support the review and approval of any documentation required by NC/CAPA deliverables.

- Mentor CAPA teams and colleagues who are beginner-level in NC/CAPA processes and systems.
Required Skills and Experience
- Quality Engineer: Systems, Assurance, or Quality Control – Minimum 4 Years experience

- Have worked in a regulated manufacturing industry: Medical devices, Pharmaceuticals, Aerospace, Automobile, Food, etc. - Minimum 4 Years

- Previous NC & CAPA and/or engineering experience and demonstrated use of quality tools/methodologies. - Minimum 4 Years of work experience

- Detailed knowledge of Quality System Regulations (21CFR820) and ISO 13485. - Minimum 3 Years

- Ability to work in a highly matrixed and geographically diverse business environment

- Quality/Compliance focus and attention to detail

- Critical thinking skills for analyzing risk, use of root cause analysis tools, and technical aptitude to collect and analyze data for determining an improvement strategy

- Expertise in cGMP and NC/CAPA documentation

- Computer skills (advanced Microsoft Office Package and statistical/data analysis and report writing skills)

- Demonstrated impactful project management and leadership skills, including the ability to lead multi-departmental project teams and resolve quality-related issues in a timely and effective manner

- Ability to work within a team and as an individual contributor in a fast-paced, changing environment

- Ability to leverage and/or engage others to accomplish projects

- Strong verbal/written communication skills with ability to communicate effectively at multiple organizational levels

- Multi-tasks, prioritizes. and meets deadlines in a timely manner

- Strong interpersonal, organizational, and follow-up skills

- Passionate about making products and processes better

Required Education and Training
- Engineering Bachelor’s degree - Preferably in science or healthcare fields.

Working Conditions
- Desk and meeting rooms

Preferred Skills and Experience
- ASQ certification : CQE, CQA, Knowledge of Process improvement tools and methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) is preferred.

- Green or Black Belt Certification in Lean or Six Sigma is a plus

- NC or CAPA Review and Approval Project Management experience

- Experience working in a broader enterprise/cross-division business unit model

jobs.title: Corporate Development Senior Manager
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
The individual in this role will manage Intuitive’s corporate development efforts for its da Vinci and Ion business units, including sourcing, investigating and negotiating a variety of transactions for the company.  Deal types will include strategic equity investments, strategic partnerships, co-marketing and co-development agreements, both in- and out-licensing, and M&A.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
- Support corporate development activities for Intuitive's da Vinci and Ion business units, including the identification, evaluation, and execution of strategic partnerships, investments, licensing transactions, and M&A opportunities.
- Identify and assess external technologies, companies, and market opportunities aligned with Intuitive's strategic priorities and technology roadmap.
- Lead or support all phases of transactions, including sourcing, relationship development, business case creation, valuation, due diligence, structuring, negotiation, contracting, integration planning, and closing.
- Manage transaction workstreams and coordinate cross-functional teams to evaluate strategic, technical, commercial, financial, legal, and regulatory considerations.
- Develop strategic assessments, financial analyses, valuation models, and recommendations to support decision-making.
- Partner with business and technology leaders to understand priorities, capability gaps, and opportunities for external innovation.
- Collaborate with Corporate Development, Strategy, Finance, Legal, and Business Unit leaders to advance opportunities aligned with corporate objectives.
- Build and maintain relationships with external companies, investors, advisors, entrepreneurs, and strategic partners.
- Prepare transaction materials and recommendations for senior leadership and executive review.
- Support and, where appropriate, lead negotiations and transaction execution activities.
- Maintain ongoing partner relationships and support post-transaction governance and integration efforts.
- Provide regular updates on active opportunities, transactions, and external relationships to Corporate Development leadership and key stakeholders.
- Perform other duties as assigned.
Core Competencies, Skills and Experience Requirements
- Minimum of 8 or more years of professional experience, with 5 or more years of experience within the medical device, life sciences, technology, finance, investing, or related industries.
- Prior work experience in corporate development, business development, finance, investing, strategy, or another relevant discipline.
- Prior experience supporting and/or executing strategic transactions, including M&A, strategic investments, licensing, partnerships, or other business development transactions. Prior experience in corporate business development is preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to evaluate new technologies, companies, markets, and strategic opportunities and assess their potential fit with broader business and technology strategies.
- Strong business judgment, analytical capabilities, results orientation, and demonstrated interest in advancing a company's strategic position through business development activities.
- Strong financial and analytical skills, including the ability to develop business cases, financial models, valuation analyses, and market assessments.
- Ability to manage key aspects of transaction execution, including opportunity assessment, business case development, due diligence, transaction structuring, negotiations, and coordination of definitive agreements.
- Ability to coordinate cross-functional teams and work effectively with stakeholders across Strategy, Finance, Legal, R&D, Marketing, Clinical, Regulatory, and other functions as appropriate.
- Strong interpersonal and influence-management skills, with the ability to build relationships, develop alignment, and move projects forward across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
- Ability to manage significant projects and workstreams with a high degree of independence while seeking guidance and alignment on key strategic and transaction decisions.
- Strong business maturity and communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with senior internal stakeholders and external executives, investors, entrepreneurs, and business partners.
- Analytical thinker who can synthesize complex information, identify the most important issues, and develop clear recommendations without becoming overly focused on unnecessary detail.
- Results-oriented, with the ability to take projects from initial evaluation through diligence, negotiation, and execution in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
- Ability to work effectively under tight deadlines and manage changing priorities while maintaining focus on key objectives.
- Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to tailor communications to different audiences.
- Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and transactions simultaneously.
- Self-motivated and proactive, with a desire to contribute to the long-term strategic success of the business.
- Ability to travel, averaging 10–20% overall. Monthly travel may range from 0% to 50%.

Education and Training Requirements
- Bachelor's degree required, preferably with relevant experience in healthcare, medical devices, life sciences, technology, finance, or a related field.
- MBA, advanced degree, or equivalent relevant professional experience preferred.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, NPI Systems
jobs.description:
rimary Function of Position
- Responsible for supply chain readiness, launch, and scale of new robotic systems platforms.
- Manages supply chain deliverables for new product introductions (NPI) of the highest value with the most complex direct materials, including supplier selection & sourcing, leading creation & adoption of category launch roadmaps, leading cross functional projects to launch & scale new products, developing & negotiating contracts, analyzing spend, creating inventory management strategies, and managing supplier performance.
- Thought leader within Global Supply Chain: develops and refines key business processes; champions and mentors team members in use of Sourcing processes; monitors industry and professional best practices

Essential Job Duties
- New Product Program Leadership & Category Management - Provides cross-functional team leadership within assigned new product program(s) of highest complexity; leads cross functional program updates, executive reviews, and alignment forums.
- Leads creation, management, and execution of program roadmaps to achieve cost, capacity, speed to market, and risk contract goals.
- Provides cross-functional team leadership within assigned category(ies) of highest complexity; leads cross-functional category team meetings

- Leads creation of long-term supplier strategies and roadmaps; able to navigate complex trade-offs in supplier strategies. Effectively influences broader organization through expert requirements gathering and leading adoption of developed strategies.
- Co-leads direct procurement supplier selection process with collaboration from Supplier Engineering. Expertly and independently deploys strategic sourcing practices to identify a core supply base able to offer lowest total cost of ownership and high-quality product while identifying value improvement opportunities.

- Supplier Performance Management

- Proactively collaborates with supply base and procurement team to understand and communicate demand changes and minimize excess inventory or material shortages during program development. Able to expertly translate business shifts and design changes to suppliers and effectively understand root cause of demand changes internally.
- Collaborate with strategic sourcing teams on shared supplier performance escalations, lead supplier escalations for new suppliers to support NPI program deliverables.
- Effectively escalates for issue resolution with supplier executive leadership. Possesses executive presence and awareness and able to drive problem resolution onsite at suppliers.

- Risk and Capacity Management

- Develops high complexity mitigation plans and programs for assigned suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers; implements plans when applicable
- Leads capacity assessments for assigned suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers; operating on three-to-five-year horizon for capacity strategies for global category and able to marshal support for proactive mitigations
- May serve as project manager for key supplier capacity or risk mitigation initiatives
- Leverages problem solving skills and develops counter-measures to implement long-term solutions to identified problems

- Contract and Cost Management

- Expert contract and cost negotiator; independently establishes contractual agreements with suppliers and amendments to existing agreements. Develops new contract language and templates as required.
- Negotiates long-term commercial agreements with executive leadership of suppliers. Installs development, cost, scale, risk mitigation and capacity agreements with key suppliers to support Intuitive’s new product introductions & volume growth.
- Leads identification and implementation of cost reduction ideas to achieve program contract cost goals.

- Acts as key thought leader within the Global Supply Chain organization through monitoring of industry and profession trends, determining, influencing, and implementing needed process improvements, and mentoring colleagues throughout the supply chain organization.
Required Skills and Experience
- Significant experience with new product introduction (NPI) in a regulated manufacturing environment
- Exceptional negotiation skills, proven track record of savings, and history of successful contract negotiations
- Significant computer experience including MS Office products and ERP systems. Strong Excel & PowerPoint skills.
- Proven track record of effective project management in a fast-paced manufacturing company. Ability to handle multiple tasks and projects successfully and adapt to changing priorities.
- Strong financial acumen; excellent working knowledge of corporate/production finance; experience building financial models and using financial knowledge to understand supplier operations
- Working knowledge of buying, material planning, master scheduling, and forecasting
- Presentation skills and the ability to make complex topics simple to drive decision making
- Demonstrates concern for precision and thoroughness
- Proven ability to consistently achieve stretch goals and objectives
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; experience presenting to senior leadership

Required Education and Training
- BS degree or equivalent and 15+ years of combined design engineering, manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, manufacturing operations, and/or supply chain experience, including at least 8 years of supply chain experience and 3 years of engineering experience, in a regulated industry manufacturing environment. Master’s degree preferred.

Working Conditions
- ~25% travel to both domestic and international suppliers

Preferred Skills and Experience
- Experience in the medical device industry or regulated manufacturing preferred.
- SAP and Agile experience preferred.
- Experience managing spend/suppliers and/or technical expertise in the following categories preferred, metals (CNC machining, aluminum castings), rapid prototyping technologies, or motion control (motors, brakes, sensors).
- Experience utilizing strategic sourcing principles, including six step sourcing process, category strategy development and adoption, and collaborative supplier management

- Ability to read and have a basic understanding of engineering drawings preferred

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position:
The Program Manager’s function is to plan, organize and lead programs and the series of projects it entails to successful completion as required by company defined key initiatives. It is also expected for this function to participate in strategic planning for the programs this position may be leading.
Roles and Responsibilities:
- Creates and manages long term goals and translates them into shorter projects to achieve the program success.
- Prepares justification for the programs he/she is managing, such as ROI, etc., to achieve buy in from top management.
- Plans, organizes and leads high scope projects.
- Leads and organizes project reviews affecting the Mexicali site.
- Prepares status reports for the projects and programs he/she is leading and be able to present at an executive level.
- Maintains budget control for projects and programs.
- Assures that proper documentation is prepared and updated to meet standards and regulations as required in a Medical device environment (FDA/ISO).
- Ability to influence others to perform needed tasks in order to ensure project completion on time and within budget.
- May require coaching other engineers in project management tools.
- Ability to lead cross functional, multisite and multicultural (both US and MX) teams.
- Create budget estimates for projects and programs.
- Performs other duties as required.
- Travel: Position may require 10-30% travel depending on the project, primarily within U.S.
Skill/Job Requirements:
Competency Requirements: (Competency is based on: education, training, skills and experience.)
In order to adequately perform the responsibilities of this position the individual must:
Required:
- Be of high character and energy with regard for detail.
- Schedule oriented and demonstrate results based on such schedules (Plans / Gantt charts)
- Highly organized with his/her tasks and tasks related to his/her programs.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal. Able to communicate eloquently up, down, and sideways.
- Demonstrate strong leadership skills to coordinate cross functional and/or multisite/multicultural teams for his/her program.
- Demonstrate site bring up and site transfer knowledge and experience.
- BS degree in an engineering discipline.
- Minimum 4 years in a Project/Program Manager role or an engineering leading role.
- Minimum 6 years mechanical, manufacturing or process engineering experience with Mid/high volume complex mechanism manufacturing.
- Possess strong communication skills to interact with suppliers and other departments within the company (product development, planning, purchasing, regulatory, quality, etc…)

Preferred:
- MS in an engineering or administration discipline.
- Project Management Certification.
- Prior responsibility for process, equipment or product validation/verification.
- Prior experience with automated equipment, complex mechanism manufacturing, or robotics.
- Experience in Just-In-Time, Demand Flow Technology, and Lean Manufacturing techniques.
- Demonstrate equipment and process validation knowledge.
- Prior experience working in an FDA/ISO regulated environment.

Language requirements:
- High English Level (+ 90 %).

jobs.title: Sr M&A Integration Manager
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
The Sr M&A Integration Manager reports to the Director, M&A Integrations and partners with Business Development, Finance, and functional teams to lead multiple transactions concurrently across the full deal lifecycle. The role leads cross-functional diligence planning and integration program management from pre-signing through close, Day 1, stabilization, and transition to the long-term business owner. Working with functional diligence leads, this person helps develop the integration strategy and milestones, consolidates integration costs, anticipates dependencies, drives execution, and provides clear recommendations to senior leadership.
Roles and Responsibilities
- Lead cross-functional diligence across Finance, Tax, Legal, HR, Regulatory, Quality, Sales & Marketing, Service, Product, Engineering/R&D, Operations, Supply Chain, IT, Security, and other relevant functions.
- Use the transaction rationale to build a diligence plan with clear workstreams, questions, owners, deliverables, dependencies, and decision dates.
- Establish diligence governance and cadence; ensure functional teams have the information, access, and direction needed to complete timely, decision-quality assessments.
- Coordinate management meetings, seller interactions, functional deep dives, data requests, and follow-ups with deal leaders and functional diligence leads. Prepare functional leads for seller engagement while preserving their ownership of functional conclusions.
- Guide functional leads, individually and collectively, to synthesize findings into an integrated view of risks, opportunities, cost, timing, resources, readiness, and integration complexity.
- Help functional leads develop the integration strategy, key milestones, and coordinated outputs that inform the deal model, purchase agreement, closing conditions, Day 1 requirements, integration roadmap, and long-term operating model.
- Build and maintain integrated plans spanning pre-close, close readiness, Day 1, cutover, stabilization, hypercare, longer-term integration, and transition to business ownership, with clear owners, milestones, dependencies, resources, and decisions.
- Lead integration cost estimation by coordinating functional inputs, reconciling assumptions, dependencies, and timing, and consolidating one-time and ongoing costs for deal and leadership decisions.
- Develop TSA scope, SLAs, schedules, and cost estimates based on the integration strategy and coordinated input from cross-functional teams.
- Partner with Legal to translate business, operational, and transaction requirements into purchase agreement terms and closing conditions and related deal documents.
- Partner with IT and functional teams to plan and execute systems integration, testing, data and process cutovers, access, business continuity, and hypercare; align technology milestones with business requirements.
- Coordinate with change-management and functional teams on organizational readiness, employee communications, Day 1, cutover, stabilization, and hypercare to support the employee experience.
- Lead multiple transactions concurrently at different lifecycle stages. Maintain visibility to milestones, risks, capacity, decisions, and cross-deal dependencies; recommend sequencing, resource allocation, and escalation when conflicts arise.
- Drive owners to complete deliverables and decisions and hold stakeholders accountable without formal authority.
- Manage risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies, and decisions. Identify slippage early, assess downstream effects, establish recovery plans, and escalate with a clear recommendation.
- Validate close-critical and Day 1 readiness. Transition ownership to business and functional leaders with clear accountabilities, open items, measures, and governance.
- Prepare concise, decision-oriented materials and present findings, readiness, risks, tradeoffs, options, and recommendations to executive sponsors, steering committees, and senior functional leaders.
- Build trusted relationships with sellers and acquired-company leaders while representing Intuitive requirements, protecting confidentiality, and maintaining transaction discipline.
- Support continuous improvement of Intuitive’s M&A diligence and integration playbooks, toolkit, templates, decision frameworks, governance, and operating rhythms. Convert retrospectives and lessons learned into practical improvements.
- Guide functional workstream leads and colleagues in effective diligence and integration practices. Use approved AI and productivity tools to improve planning, synthesis, reporting, and portfolio visibility while protecting confidential information.
Required Skills and Experience
- Minimum of 12 years of related experience
- Deep understanding of the M&A lifecycle, including transaction evaluation, diligence, signing, close preparation, Day 1, stabilization, post-close execution, and transition to business ownership.
- Significant experience leading cross-functional M&A diligence and integration, rather than participating solely as a functional contributor.
- Substantial experience leading buy-side M&A diligence and integrations in complex, global, or highly regulated environments.
- Proven ability to coordinate multidisciplinary teams and connect business, financial, legal, technical, operational, people, regulatory, and quality findings into an integrated point of view.
- Experience supporting transaction-structure decisions, transition service agreements, current- and future-state operating models, and value-realization tracking.
- Experience working directly with target-company leadership, executive sponsors, and senior internal stakeholders.
- Strong dependency, critical-path, and portfolio-management judgment, including prioritization across competing deals and functional capacity constraints.
- Ability to create structure in ambiguity, make progress with incomplete information, and determine when to use a standard approach, adapt it, or escalate.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a record of recovering slipping plans, resolving cross-functional impasses, accelerating decisions, and driving deliverables to completion.
- Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to drive decisions at all levels by simplifying complex issues, clarifying tradeoffs and implications, and making credible recommendations.
- Strong facilitation, negotiation, diplomacy, and influence skills; ability to align stakeholders and drive outcomes without direct authority.
- Discretion and sound judgment when handling confidential transaction information.
- Must be comfortable using approved AI tools to improve workflows across deal lifecycle and personal productivity while protecting confidential information.
- Ability to travel up to 25% domestically and internationally based on transaction needs.
- Comfort working across global time zones and cultures, with flexibility to support transaction timelines and geographically distributed stakeholders.
- This role requires working onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday every week.

Required Education and Training
- Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, engineering, operations, life sciences, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

Preferred Skills and Experience
- MBA or other relevant advanced degree.
- Experience in medical technology, healthcare, life sciences, diagnostics, or another regulated technology industry.
- Cross-border transaction experience and understanding of the legal, employment, regulatory, tax, trade, quality, technology, commercial, and operational factors that shape deals
- Experience supporting software, SaaS, or technology-enabled acquisitions by enabling the back-office capabilities needed to support product teams, including cybersecurity, licensing, systems, and related operational requirements.
- Experience improving diligence frameworks, integration playbooks, governance, executive reporting, or reusable tools.
- Demonstrated outcomes such as improved readiness, risk mitigation, faster decisions, operational continuity, talent retention, fulfillment of closing requirements, or achievement of integration objectives.

Primary Function of Position:
The Sr Sales Strategy Analyst will partner closely with US commercial leadership to analyze complex business challenges, providing strategic, data-driven insights that directly influence critical business decisions. The Senior Analyst will build strong, strategic business partner relationships with the executive commercial leadership of two regions within the US.
This is a highly analytical and consultative role that works extensively with large, dynamic datasets to support commercial strategy, performance optimization, and customer targeting. The ideal candidate will have strong technical and analytical skills, enabling them to consolidate disparate data sources, identify critical business drivers, and effectively communicate with and influence key stakeholders.
Roles and Responsibilities:
- Drive actionable insights through proactively identifying emerging business trends, risks and opportunities, and delivering recommendations that inform strategic decisions.
- Build a deep understanding of business drivers and trends with the ability to translate data analyses into actionable insights that influence executive decision-making.
- Serve as a strategic advisor and trusted partner to multiple VP & Director level business partners,
- leveraging advanced data analytics to drive key business strategies.
- Clearly articulate and confidently defend data-driven, strategic recommendations
- Proactively identify and lead initiatives to improve internal processes and scale business insights
- Drive and enhance recurring quarterly deliverables for the US clinical business, such as executive reporting packages, sales performance reporting, territory design, and quota modeling and allocation.

- Minimum of 5 years of work experience in sales operations, business intelligence, sales strategy, business operations, or a similar analytical role.
- Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to simplify the complex.

- Self-motivated to seek out resolutions, resources, and share knowledge.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Systems
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position:
The Program is responsible for leading and executing the full product development lifecycle of medical device capital systems, from initial concept through commercial launch. This role requires deep expertise in medical device development, regulatory pathways, operations, and cross-functional project management. The Program Manager serves as a key driver of product innovation, compliance, and operational excellence within the organization. The Program Manager provides strategic leadership and tactical execution across all stages of product development, including concept generation, design, prototyping, verification and validation, regulatory submissions, manufacturing transfer, and launch. The role is pivotal in ensuring that all products meet stringent compliance requirements, including FDA, EU MDR, ISO standards, and relevant quality system regulations.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Strategic Leadership
- Partner with product, technical, and functional leaders to shape program strategy, roadmap priorities, and execution plans.
- Align engineering, clinical, operations, regulatory, and product teams to meet program and portfolio goals.
- Facilitate program reviews and structured decisions to resolve issues, balance trade-offs, and maintain momentum.
- Lead cross-functional negotiations, resolve root-cause disputes, and build sustainable stakeholder alignment.
- Create concise executive narratives and reports that integrate analysis, recommendations, risks, and trade-offs.

Product & Design Development
- Lead cross-functional teams through concept development, design iteration, prototyping, verification/validation, and design transfer to manufacturing.
- Resolve cross-functional dependencies across subsystem teams, external partners, manufacturing, regulatory, and commercial functions.
- Partner with design, clinical, human factors, and engineering teams to ensure product requirements, usability, and performance criteria are met.
- Lead design control and business reviews, ensuring governance, compliance, accountability, and timely escalation.

Operational Execution
- Drive manufacturing readiness, including process development, supply chain coordination, build readiness, and launch planning.
- Ensure smooth transition from R&D to operations with strong cross-functional integration and documentation rigor.
- Support ongoing product lifecycle, cost reductions, reliability improvements, and sustainment workstreams.
- Partner with Finance to monitor program budgets, resource allocation, and long-term financial impacts.
- Manage scope across projects, evaluating strategic alignment, delivery impact, dependencies, and trade-offs.
- Optimize WBS and program schedules across interdependent projects, including critical and near-critical path analysis.

Regulatory & Compliance
- Ensure project deliverables meet relevant US and global medical device standards and quality system requirements.
- Coordinate cross-functional preparation of regulatory documentation and testing.
- Champion strong design controls, risk management, and audit-ready documentation throughout the lifecycle.
- Anticipate systemic regulatory, financial, operational, and technical risks; drive cross-functional response plans.
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
Required:
- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical or Biomedical Engineering or a related technical field; advanced degree preferred.
- At least a minimum of 10 years' experience leading complex medical device development programs, including capital equipment or system-level products, from concept through commercial launch.
- In-depth knowledge of medical device regulatory pathways (FDA, EU MDR, ISO 13485), submission requirements, and quality system regulations.
- Proven ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams at multiple levels of the organization.
- Experience collaborating with engineering, operations, regulatory, quality, and clinical teams throughout all development phases.
- Exceptional communication and stakeholder-management skills.
- Ability to handle ambiguity effectively and oversee multiple large projects at once
- Advanced program planning skills, including WBS, dependency management, critical path analysis, scope control, risk management, and governance reporting.
- Ability to coach peers on stakeholder engagement, communication, scheduling discipline, and program management tools.
- Experience evaluating trade-offs across product features, customer needs, manufacturability, and cost.

Preferred:
- Experience in robotic surgery, software/mechanical/electrical/optical technology based products and design transfer to manufacturing and service organizations.
- PMP certification or formal project management training.
- Familiarity with ALM/PLM systems, Agile methodologies, and project management tools.
- Start-up experience a plus.

jobs.title: Director Finance AI & Data Governance
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
The Director, Finance AI and Data Governance will lead Finance-wide AI transformation by building trusted data foundations, governed semantic layers, and scalable AI capabilities that improve decision-making, productivity, controls, and business partnership. This leader will define and execute the Finance AI strategy, operating model, governance framework, and value-realization approach in close partnership with Finance leadership, Enterprise AI and Data, IT, and other enterprise partners.
The role owns Finance data governance, semantic modeling, AI agent development and design standards, use case prioritization, adoption, and measurable value delivery across financial and operational domains. This leader will establish and lead a central team of AI and data experts that shapes the future of Finance through governed, scalable, AI-driven transformation.
Roles and Responsibilities
- Own the Finance AI and data transformation roadmap in support of the Finance team vision.

- Translate Finance strategy into a prioritized portfolio of AI and data initiatives that accelerate planning and reporting cycles, improve forecast accuracy, reduce manual work, strengthen controls, and enhance decision support.

- Establish Finance data governance policies in partnership with Enterprise AI and Data to ensure a single source of truth, high-quality data foundations, and scalable capabilities that support business needs and future growth.

- Lead governance forums that approve definitions, business rules, quality standards, lineage expectations, security, and access controls.

- Own the Finance semantic layer and certified metric framework, standardizing definitions and calculation logic across reporting, analytics, planning, and AI agents.

- Establish certification, release, version control, and change-management processes for the Finance semantic layer.

- Define the playbook for Finance agents, including grounding, orchestration, evaluation, testing, deployment, and monitoring.

- Own the operating model for democratized agent development and ensure approved semantic models and governed data are developed to support scaling AI within Finance.

- Establish accuracy thresholds, human oversight, risk controls, and production support expectations.

- Lead the intake and prioritization process across Finance AI and Data initiatives, including capacity allocation and recurring portfolio reviews with Finance leadership.

- Lead the operating model for Finance AI and data delivery by setting standards, enabling functional teams, managing portfolio trade-offs, and ensuring central capabilities are adopted consistently across Finance.

- Build, lead, and develop a central Finance AI and Data Governance team, including talent strategy, operating cadence, delivery expectations, and collaboration norms with functional Finance teams.

- Partner with IT, Enterprise AI and Data, Security, and Finance leadership to align architecture, responsible AI practices, investment priorities, implementation roadmaps, and executive governance.

- Build a Finance AI community of practice, champion network, role-based learning plan, and reusable playbooks to scale AI proficiency across the finance organization.

- Partner with functional leaders to leverage AI to improve day-to-day work, and transform business processes.

- Measure adoption, productivity, quality, value realization, and risk posture across the AI and data portfolio.

- Serve as a trusted advisor to the Finance organization and enterprise partners. Translate the portfolio into measurable outcomes, communicate progress and risks to governance forums, and ensure investment decisions remain aligned to Finance strategy and enterprise architecture.
Required Skills and Experience
- Minimum of 12 years of progressive leadership experience across Finance, FP&A, data and analytics, digital transformation, AI, data governance or related disciplines.
- Demonstrated success leading cross-functional enterprise programs and influencing senior stakeholders.
- Strong understanding of Finance processes, controls, performance management, and financial and operational metrics.
- Experience establishing data governance, semantic models, analytics products, or AI-enabled solutions.
- Ability to translate business strategy into an executable portfolio, operating model, and measurable outcomes.
- Experience leading organizational change, adoption, and capability building in Finance.
- Enterprise thinker who can connect data, technology, controls, and Finance outcomes.
- Product-oriented leader who prioritizes user value and scalable capabilities over one-off solutions.
- Strong governance judgment with the ability to enable innovation while maintaining trust and control.
- Clear executive communicator who can simplify complex AI and data concepts.
- Ability to attract and retain top talent, drive innovation, and create accountability across dotted-line teams.
- Experience with modern data and analytics platforms such as Snowflake and Databricks.
- Experience with enterprise generative AI, agentic solutions, responsible AI practices, or model evaluation.
- Knowledge of enterprise planning and ERP platforms such as Anaplan and SAP.
- This role requires working onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday every week

Required Education and Training
- Bachelor's degree in finance, computer science, mathematics, information systems or business.

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
We are seeking an experienced Senior Program Manager to oversee and drive cross-functional development programs for small molecule therapeutics. This role will provide leadership and coordination across CMC, non-clinical, clinical, and regulatory functions, ensuring that programs are executed on time, within budget, and in compliance with global regulatory standards.
The Senior Program Manager will serve as the primary point of accountability for assigned programs, leading integrated teams, and reporting progress and risks to executive leadership. The ideal candidate brings broad drug development expertise, strong organizational skills, and the ability to influence and motivate diverse stakeholders to achieve program goals.
Roles and Responsibilities
- Lead cross-functional teams through all stages of small molecule drug development, from preclinical through late-stage clinical studies
- Drive end-to-end program lifecycle – initiation to closure – ensuring stakeholder alignment and objective clarity
- Oversee CMC timelines and deliverable completion for activities that include process development, manufacturing, analytical methods, formulation, stability, and clinical supply readiness across multiple suppliers to ensure that materials are delivered on time and within budget
- Coordinate with Nonclinical activities such as toxicology, PK/PD, safety pharmacology, and ADME studies to enable on time regulatory submissions

- Experience with CMC, regulatory submissions, clinical operations, and non-clinical activities.
- Strong understanding of the drug development lifecycle, from discovery through commercialization.
- Familiarity with global regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, ICH guidelines) and compliance standards (GxP).
- Advanced program management skills with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and scenario planning.
- Ability to communicate complex issues clearly to both technical teams and executive leadership.

Primary Function of Position
The Corporate Development Director - Digital Product role leads corporate development for Intuitive’s Digital business unit, translating the Digital strategy into external growth opportunities. The role owns the transaction lifecycle—from sourcing and evaluation through negotiation, closing, and integration planning—across strategic equity investments, partnerships, co-marketing and co-development agreements, in- and out-licensing, and M&A. Success requires close partnership with Digital, Strategy, Finance, Legal, and other business leaders to advance Intuitive’s technology platforms, products, and long-term strategic position.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
•    Lead cross-functional evaluation of external technology opportunities for strategic, commercial, and product fit with Intuitive’s Digital business.

•    Own transactions end to end, including outreach, business cases, structuring, negotiation, due diligence, contracting, integration planning, and closing.

•    Partner with product and technology teams to understand roadmaps, priorities, capability gaps, and external development needs.

•    Partner with Strategy, Finance, and business leaders to shape and execute M&A strategy for Digital technologies.

•    Represent Intuitive’s strategic interests externally and provide senior leaders and the Board with deal updates, recommendations, risks, and decisions required.

•    Manage post-transaction partner relationships to support strategic objectives, governance, and integration or collaboration plans.

•    Keep stakeholders informed of transaction status, partner relationships, key risks, upcoming decisions, and required actions.

•    Perform other duties as assigned.
Core Competencies, Skills and Experience Requirements
•    Ten (10+) or more years of professional experience, seven (7) or more years’ experience within the medical device, life sciences industry, or technology.

•    Experience developing or selling healthcare data analytics products preferred.

•    Prior work experience must be in finance, investing or other relevant discipline

•    Prior transactional experience including required. Prior experience in corporate business development is strongly preferred.

•    Proven track record of advancement within the medical device, life sciences or investing industry.

•    Keen business intuition, results orientation, negotiation skills and demonstrated interest in advancing a business’ strategic position through business development activities.

•    Strong detail-orientation, as well as the ability to interact with several internal functions and build a consensus from a varied group of departments and individuals.

•    Ability to achieve significant objectives and drive major projects, with limited authority.  Outstanding teamwork and influence-management skills with the ability to successfully work with others at all levels

•    Strong leadership skills, and the business maturity, intellect and integrity required to establish immediate credibility with external constituencies.

•    Analytic thinker who approaches problems logically without getting lost in the detail or suffering from “analysis/paralysis”.

•    Ability to develop market and financial models.

•    Results oriented, with the ability to lead a project from its very early inception, and to motivate all players, internal and external, to bring the project to a mutually beneficial completion.

•    Sustainable ability to work under tight deadlines and to remain focused on objectives whether deadline pressure is on or off.

•    Outstanding communication skills, including orally, in writing or presentation format.  Ability to appropriately modify communications depending upon the audience.

•    Strong organizational and prioritization skills with the ability to manage multiple projects on an ongoing basis.

•    Self-motivation driven by the desire to make an impact on the long-term success of the business.

•    Ability to travel, averaging 10 – 20% overall.  However, monthly travel may range from 0% to 50%.
Education and Training Requirements
•    Bachelor’s degree with clinical and/or healthcare industry experience, MBA or Ph.D. preferred.

jobs.title: Clinical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position:
The Senior Clinical Program Manager serves as the strategic and operational partner to Clinical Development & Operations leadership, providing integrated program management across the Clinical Development & Operations portfolio from study startup through regulatory submission. The role partners with Clinical Development & Operations leadership to inform Clinical Development & Operations strategy through integrated planning, scenario analysis, governance, and execution insights, translating strategic direction into coordinated cross-functional plans that enable successful program execution.
Reporting to the Program Management & Operations organization, the Senior Clinical Program Manager partners across Clinical Development & Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs, CMC, Nonclinical, Quality, Commercial, and external partners to integrate timelines, risks, dependencies, and key decisions into unified program plans. In partnership with Enterprise Program Management, the role establishes Clinical Development & Operations governance and ensures cross-functional risks, dependencies, and decision requests are appropriately elevated through enterprise governance to support informed decision-making and coordinated execution.
Roles and Responsibilities
- Support the Program Management & Operations team in creating and implementing Clinical Development & Operations governance processes, including governance forums, operating cadences, decision pathways, program reporting, and the RAID framework.
- Facilitate Clinical Development & Operations & Operations governance by preparing governance materials, maintaining clinical RAID and decision logs, capturing actions and decisions, monitoring follow-through, and escalating cross-functional risks and decision requests through enterprise governance, as appropriate.
- Develop, maintain, and communicate integrated timelines across the clinical portfolio, ensuring alignment of milestones, dependencies, critical path activities, and cross-functional deliverables.
- Coordinate program-level execution across Study Leads, Clinical Operations, Data Management, Biostatistics, Safety, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Writing, Quality, and external partners, providing hands-on project management support to individual studies as needed.
- Monitor portfolio execution, proactively identifying schedule impacts, resource constraints, cross-study dependencies, and operational risks, and facilitate development of mitigation plans.
- Develop executive-ready portfolio reporting that communicates program health, milestone performance, critical path status, key risks, decision requests, and recommended actions.
- Identify portfolio trends and opportunities to strengthen planning, governance, reporting, and operational effectiveness across Clinical Development & Operations.
- Support regular functional-area budget management in coordination with Clinical Development & Operations Functional Area Team Leads and PM&O by tracking actual and forecasted accruals, invoices, purchase orders, and inputs to the Annual Operations Budget Planning Cycle.
- Support CRO and Vendor oversight by: incorporating vendor updates into project plans and governance materials; maintaining visibility and supporting management of purchase orders, change orders, invoices, key contract terms, and performance commitments; and coordinating business reviews and operational follow-up across internal functions.
- Drive adoption of standardized project management tools, templates, dashboards, reporting practices, and workflow automation that improve portfolio visibility, consistency, and execution.
Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Pharma/Life Sciences, or a related field (or equivalent experience). An advanced degree is preferred.
- Minimum 10 years of program or project management experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or CRO industry supporting Clinical Development & Operations through NDA regulatory submissions.
- Demonstrated success leading cross-functional planning and execution across multiple concurrent clinical studies, including integrated planning, critical path management, and dependency management.
- Experience partnering with Clinical Development & Operations, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, and Quality leadership to support governance, portfolio planning, and executive decision-making.
- Experience supporting late-stage Clinical Development & Operations programs and familiarity with Clinical Development & Operations processes from start-up through close-out.
- Expertise in integrated timeline management, risk and issue management, resource coordination, and cross-functional execution.
- Strong executive communication and presentation skills, with the ability to deliver clear, actionable recommendations to senior leadership; High emotional intelligence and the ability to build trusted partnerships across technical and business functions.
- Proficiency with Smartsheet, including integrated project planning, dashboards, reporting, and workflow automation.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience working with CROs, vendors, and cross-functional development teams
- PMP or comparable project management certification.
- Familiarity with procurement, contract, and financial management systems (e.g., Coupa, iValua, SAP, Ariba, or equivalent).

jobs.description:

Responsibilities include supporting Intuitive’s Environmental Management System with delivery and execution of related projects including the administration and maturity of Restricted/Regulated Substance Database, Battery and Packaging program management, collaboration tools and development of operational reports and tools for use by the broader functional and regional teams. Skills

- Exceptional organizational, data entry, decision making and analytical skills.

- Demonstrated self-starting, results driven, high energy level and ability to focus

- Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
The Director, Corporate Development Finance acts as the Finance leader for initiatives originating from our Corporate Development organization. This role also serves as a resource to support senior executives engaged in strategic investments across the business.
Roles & Responsibilities
- Serve as an expert focused on evaluating a broad range of growth opportunities for Intuitive in support of Sr. Director, Corporate Development & Sales Operations.

- Operate as a player coach while managing a team of managers and analysts who support our Corporate Development initiatives.

- Collaborate with deal champions and deal teams to research markets, technologies and organizations to assess strategic fit, build/buy/partner options, and financial value.

- Partner with deal champions and deal teams on identifying and diligencing areas that impact valuation and transaction structure for M&A and BD deals.

- Develop and own financial models and valuation analyses in support of M&A and BD deals (acquisitions, licenses, equity investments, joint ventures, partnerships, etc.).

- Evaluating deal structure options in partnership with the deal champions and deal teams.

- Coordinate across Business Unit leaders, Functional leaders, and the broader Finance organization in developing deal models and translating them into core operational processes.

- Develop board-level presentation materials in support of M&A and BD deals.

- Track and report return on investments made in external organizations.

- 15+ years of relevant experience in medical device focused Corporate Development, Investment Banking, Equity Research, Buy Side, or Venture Capital roles.
- 10+ years of experience in leading deal teams to develop M&A models, execute on VC investments, lead diligence processes, and provide Intrinsic/Relative value perspectives.
- Desire to work in a dynamic, fast-paced organization.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Intellectual curiosity and ability to navigate ambiguous circumstances.
- Exceptional analytical and critical thinking skills.

- This role requires working onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday every week

- Bachelor’s degree (MBA preferred)

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, NPI Sourcing
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
- Responsible for supply chain readiness, launch, and scale of new robotic systems platforms.
- Manages supply chain deliverables for new product introductions (NPI) of the highest value with the most complex direct materials, including supplier selection & sourcing, leading creation & adoption of category launch roadmaps, leading cross functional projects to launch & scale new products, developing & negotiating contracts, analyzing spend, creating inventory management strategies, and managing supplier performance.
- Thought leader within Global Supply Chain: develops and refines key business processes; champions and mentors team members in use of Sourcing processes; monitors industry and professional best practices

Essential Job Duties
- New Product Program Leadership & Category Management - Provides cross-functional team leadership within assigned new product program(s) of highest complexity; leads cross functional program updates, executive reviews, and alignment forums.
- Leads creation, management, and execution of program roadmaps to achieve cost, capacity, speed to market, and risk contract goals.
- Provides cross-functional team leadership within assigned category(ies) of highest complexity; leads cross-functional category team meetings

- Leads creation of long-term supplier strategies and roadmaps; able to navigate complex trade-offs in supplier strategies. Effectively influences broader organization through expert requirements gathering and leading adoption of developed strategies.
- Co-leads direct procurement supplier selection process with collaboration from Supplier Engineering. Expertly and independently deploys strategic sourcing practices to identify a core supply base able to offer lowest total cost of ownership and high-quality product while identifying value improvement opportunities.

- Supplier Performance Management
- Proactively collaborates with supply base and procurement team to understand and communicate demand changes and minimize excess inventory or material shortages during program development. Able to expertly translate business shifts and design changes to suppliers and effectively understand root cause of demand changes internally.
- Collaborate with strategic sourcing teams on shared supplier performance escalations, lead supplier escalations for new suppliers to support NPI program deliverables.
- Effectively escalates for issue resolution with supplier executive leadership. Possesses executive presence and awareness and able to drive problem resolution onsite at suppliers.

- Risk and Capacity Management

- Develops high complexity mitigation plans and programs for assigned suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers; implements plans when applicable
- Leads capacity assessments for assigned suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers; operating on three-to-five-year horizon for capacity strategies for global category and able to marshal support for proactive mitigations
- May serve as project manager for key supplier capacity or risk mitigation initiatives
- Leverages problem solving skills and develops counter-measures to implement long-term solutions to identified problems

- Contract and Cost Management

- Expert contract and cost negotiator; independently establishes contractual agreements with suppliers and amendments to existing agreements. Develops new contract language and templates as required.
- Negotiates long-term commercial agreements with executive leadership of suppliers. Installs development, cost, scale, risk mitigation and capacity agreements with key suppliers to support Intuitive’s new product introductions & volume growth.
- Leads identification and implementation of cost reduction ideas to achieve program contract cost goals.

- Acts as key thought leader within the Global Supply Chain organization through monitoring of industry and profession trends, determining, influencing, and implementing needed process improvements, and mentoring colleagues throughout the supply chain organization.
Required Skills and Experience
- Significant experience with new product introduction (NPI) in a regulated manufacturing environment
- Exceptional negotiation skills, proven track record of savings, and history of successful contract negotiations
- Significant computer experience including MS Office products and ERP systems. Strong Excel & PowerPoint skills.
- Proven track record of effective project management in a fast-paced manufacturing company. Ability to handle multiple tasks and projects successfully and adapt to changing priorities.
- Strong financial acumen; excellent working knowledge of corporate/production finance; experience building financial models and using financial knowledge to understand supplier operations
- Working knowledge of buying, material planning, master scheduling, and forecasting
- Presentation skills and the ability to make complex topics simple to drive decision making
- Demonstrates concern for precision and thoroughness
- Proven ability to consistently achieve stretch goals and objectives
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; experience presenting to senior leadership

Required Education and Training
- BS degree or equivalent and 15+ years of combined design engineering, manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, manufacturing operations, and/or supply chain experience, including at least 8 years of supply chain experience and 3 years of engineering experience, in a regulated industry manufacturing environment. Master’s degree preferred.

Working Conditions
- ~25% travel to both domestic and international suppliers

Preferred Skills and Experience
- Experience in the medical device industry or regulated manufacturing preferred.
- SAP and Agile experience preferred.
- Experience managing spend/suppliers and/or technical expertise in the following categories preferred, metals (CNC machining, aluminum castings), rapid prototyping technologies, or motion control (motors, brakes, sensors).
- Experience utilizing strategic sourcing principles, including six step sourcing process, category strategy development and adoption, and collaborative supplier management
- Certifications: CPSM, CPIM, and/or PMP preferred.
- Ability to read and have a basic understanding of engineering drawings preferred
- Basic understanding of data visualization tools (similar to Tableau, Power BI etc.) preferred
- Experience with make vs. buy decisions & ROI analysis preferred
- Knowledge of Cost of Goods Sold (COGs) and cost levers preferred

jobs.title: Director, Finance India
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position:
The Director, Finance India leads the India finance organization. This leader is the advisor and business partner for the VP and General Manager of India. Responsible for all finance and sales operations-related matters in the market, including partnering with the Asia finance leadership team to deliver outstanding financial performance, budgeting, forecasting, closing activities, analytics, quotas, reporting, customer targeting, proper financial governance and controllership.  Will be tasked with analyzing complex business problems and providing strategic, data-driven recommendations that support planning, commercial strategy, short and long-range financial models, and accelerated da Vinci adoption in the region.
This is a highly analytical role requiring a keen understanding of commercial finance and accounting concepts, analytic processes, the ability to lead and motivate multiple teams, and the ability to communicate and develop meaningful work relationships with multiple executive business partners.
Roles and Responsibilities
- Lead and develop the India finance, accounting, and sales operations teams with specific focus on the organization / team in India.
- Serve as the primary Finance/Sales Operations strategic advisor for the VP and GM of India.
- Responsible for all India finance-related and sales operations activity, including: - Budgets, forecasts, closing activities, analytics/insight generation, quota development, P&L management, sales commission plans, commercial and financial reporting, customer targeting, financial governance, cash management and accounting.

- Analyze complex business problems and issues using data from internal and external sources to provide insights, identify patterns, and inform resource allocation decisions to executive leadership.
- Provide early insights regarding market trends and the resultant strategic/business model impact.
- Support development of regional goals and provide reporting on progress towards goals.
- Lead closing activities and ensure US GAAP and statutory reporting requirements are properly met.
- Work with Corporate tax team and ensure all Tax requirements are met.
- Work with corporate treasury on cash management.
- Partner with Executive commercial leadership to develop board-level presentation materials.
- Use analytical skills to verify or dispel anecdotal insights.
- Take ownership and lead the financial evaluation for any key important business investments in India.
Skill / Job Requirements
- Strong ability and track record of developing, leading, motivating large teams.
- Strong financial and problem-solving skills and ability to think critically through complexity.
- High curiosity and aptitude for understanding trends, outliers, and causal relationships.
- Highly-organized with an ability to support and prioritize multiple projects concurrently.
- Excellent written and oral communication with a dedicated customer orientation.
- Strong understanding of US GAAP and relevant controllership experience (including statutory accounting, Credit & Collections, Accounts Payable, intercompany, VAT, and local tax and customs requirements and audits)
- Proficiency with dashboard/report creation and data visualization tools (Tableau preferred)
- Advanced Excel skills (SQL or other database preferred)
- Bachelor’s degree (Masters degree preferred)
- Availability for travel abroad as requested.
- 15 or more years of relevant work experience.

models.

- Advanced MS Office skills (MS Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel)

- Working knowledge of buying, material planning, master scheduling,

and forecasting.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills is required. Ability to

communicate both at the high (strategic) and detailed (tactical) level

- Ability to handle multiple tasks and projects successfully.

suppliers.

jobs.title: Program Manager,  NPI Sourcing
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
- Responsible for supply chain readiness, launch, and scale of new instrument or system platforms.
- Manages supply chain deliverables for new product introductions (NPI) of the highest value with the most complex direct materials, including supplier selection & sourcing, leading creation & adoption of category launch roadmaps, leading cross functional projects to launch & scale new products, developing & negotiating contracts, analyzing spend, creating inventory management strategies, and managing supplier performance.
- Thought leader within Global Supply Chain: develops and refines key business processes; champions and mentors team members in use of Sourcing processes; monitors industry and professional best practices

Essential Job Duties
- New Product Program Leadership & Category Management - Provides cross-functional team leadership within assigned new product program(s) of highest complexity; leads cross functional program updates, executive reviews, and alignment forums.
- Leads creation, management, and execution of program roadmaps to achieve cost, capacity, speed to market, and risk contract goals.
- Provides cross-functional team leadership within assigned category(ies) of highest complexity; leads cross-functional category team meetings
- Leads creation of long-term supplier strategies and roadmaps; able to navigate complex trade-offs in supplier strategies. Effectively influences broader organization through expert requirements gathering and leading adoption of developed strategies.
- Co-leads direct procurement supplier selection process with collaboration from Supplier Engineering. Expertly and independently deploys strategic sourcing practices to identify a core supply base able to offer lowest total cost of ownership and high-quality product while identifying value improvement opportunities.

- Supplier Performance Management - Proactively collaborates with supply base and procurement team to understand and communicate demand changes and minimize excess inventory or material shortages during program development. Able to expertly translate business shifts and design changes to suppliers and effectively understand root cause of demand changes internally.
- Collaborate with strategic sourcing teams on shared supplier performance escalations, lead supplier escalations for new suppliers to support NPI program deliverables.
- Effectively escalates for issue resolution with supplier executive leadership. Possesses executive presence and awareness and able to drive problem resolution onsite at suppliers.

- Risk and Capacity Management - Develops high complexity mitigation plans and programs for assigned suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers; implements plans when applicable
- Leads capacity assessments for assigned suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers; operating on three-to-five-year horizon for capacity strategies for global category and able to marshal support for proactive mitigations
- May serve as project manager for key supplier capacity or risk mitigation initiatives
- Leverages problem solving skills and develops counter-measures to implement long-term solutions to identified problems

- Contract and Cost Management - Expert contract and cost negotiator; independently establishes contractual agreements with suppliers and amendments to existing agreements. Develops new contract language and templates as required.
- Negotiates long-term commercial agreements with executive leadership of suppliers. Installs development, cost, scale, risk mitigation and capacity agreements with key suppliers to support Intuitive’s new product introductions & volume growth.
- Leads identification and implementation of cost reduction ideas to achieve program contract cost goals.

- Acts as key thought leader within the Global Supply Chain organization through monitoring of industry and profession trends, determining, influencing, and implementing needed process improvements, and mentoring colleagues throughout the supply chain organization.
Required Skills and Experience
- Significant experience with new product introduction (NPI) in a regulated manufacturing environment
- Exceptional negotiation skills, proven track record of savings, and history of successful contract negotiations
- Significant computer experience including MS Office products and ERP systems. Strong Excel & PowerPoint skills.
- Proven track record of effective project management in a fast-paced manufacturing company. Ability to handle multiple tasks and projects successfully and adapt to changing priorities.
- Strong financial acumen; excellent working knowledge of corporate/production finance; experience building financial models and using financial knowledge to understand supplier operations
- Working knowledge of buying, material planning, master scheduling, and forecasting
- Presentation skills and the ability to make complex topics simple to drive decision making
- Demonstrates concern for precision and thoroughness
- Proven ability to consistently achieve stretch goals and objectives
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; experience presenting to senior leadership

Required Education and Training
- BS degree or equivalent and 15+ years of combined design engineering, manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, manufacturing operations, and/or supply chain experience, including at least 8 years of supply chain experience and 3 years of engineering experience, in a regulated industry manufacturing environment. Master’s degree preferred.

Working Conditions
- ~25% travel to both domestic and international suppliers

Preferred Skills and Experience
- Experience in the medical device industry or regulated manufacturing preferred.
- SAP and Agile experience preferred.
- Experience managing spend/suppliers and/or technical expertise in the following categories preferred, metals (CNC machining, aluminum castings), rapid prototyping technologies, or motion control (motors, brakes, sensors).
- Experience utilizing strategic sourcing principles, including six step sourcing process, category strategy development and adoption, and collaborative supplier management
- Certifications: CPSM, CPIM, and/or PMP preferred.
- Ability to read and have a basic understanding of engineering drawings preferred
- Basic understanding of data visualization tools (similar to Tableau, Power BI etc.) preferred
- Experience with make vs. buy decisions & ROI analysis preferred
- Knowledge of Cost of Goods Sold (COGs) and cost levers preferred

- Proven ability to consistently achieve stretch goals and objectives
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; experience presenting to senior leadership

Master’s degree preferred.

jobs.title: Physician - Corporate Strategy
jobs.description:
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, clinical, product, regulatory, reimbursement, and strategy partners to determine which opportunities should advance and how they should be clinically and commercially framed.

Essential Job Duties
- Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
- Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
- Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.
- Partner with engineering and design teams to define clinical use cases, procedural workflows, performance goals, and prototype feedback loops for new platforms.
- Lead or support early clinical de-risking activities, including preclinical studies, simulated use, workflow validation, and early feasibility planning where appropriate.
- Develop point-of-view assessments on emerging technologies, startups, venture-backed innovation, adjacent markets, and external partnership opportunities.
- Collaborate with regulatory, reimbursement, health economics, product, and commercial strategy partners to shape indication strategy and development pathways.
- Engage KOLs, clinicians, entrepreneurs, academic innovators, and external partners to validate concepts and inform investment decisions.
- Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.
Experience and Qualifications
- MD or DO required; active clinical practice is valued but not required for candidates with substantial innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
- Must demonstrate at least one of the following experience profiles: (1) meaningful hands-on clinical practice or procedural care experience plus exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) strong venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, corporate strategy, or product strategy experience plus sufficient clinical fluency to evaluate medical needs and care pathways.
- Ability to identify unmet clinical needs and convert observations into structured hypotheses, need statements, development plans, or investment theses.
- Experience conducting clinician, patient, or stakeholder interviews and synthesizing voice-of-customer input into actionable product or strategy recommendations.
- Comfort operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments where the path forward is uncertain and evidence must be built iteratively.
- Strong cross-functional influence skills and ability to collaborate with engineering, clinical, regulatory, reimbursement, product, and business stakeholders.
- Ability to evaluate clinical workflows, procedure economics, adoption barriers, competitive dynamics, and strategic implications for new technology platforms.
- Clear executive communication skills, including crisp written synthesis, structured presentations, and the ability to explain complex clinical concepts to non-clinical audiences.
- Curiosity, ownership mindset, and enthusiasm for building new technologies that can transform care delivery and improve patient outcomes.
- Biodesign or equivalent needs-based innovation training preferred; experience in venture, startups, business development, product strategy, or corporate strategy strongly preferred.

The product portfolio will include da Vinci systems, Advanced Technologies, Instruments and Accessories and Digital Solutions including Intuitive Hub, My Intuitive and SIMNOW.
You will be responsible for developing value messaging, KOL development and scaling the success of existing and newly launched products while accelerating the adoption of Intuitive’s product and digital portfolios across the UK and Ireland.
